niche_preference_profile: This user prefers clean, modern, app-like interfaces with strong hierarchy, clear labels, and enough content to feel complete, but not so much density that the screen feels crowded. They like light, airy layouts in general, though they also respond well to dark, high-contrast alert states when the context is urgent. They favor concise, direct copy, prominent primary actions, and organized sections with consistent spacing and polished card styling.

criteria.description: Prefers layouts with a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy, strong title prominence, and obvious section structure.
Prefers interfaces that feel uncluttered, with fewer visible controls, less visual noise, and simpler surrounding chrome.
Prefers generous, even spacing and breathing room between sections rather than cramped or tightly stacked content.
Prefers clean, finished, intentional card treatments that feel modern and app-like rather than heavy or dashboard-like.
Prefers short, direct, informative copy over verbose, conversational, or overly explanatory text.
Prefers a prominent, easy-to-spot primary CTA with strong visual emphasis and clear action affordance.
Prefers settings and controls organized into a small number of clear sections or blocks rather than many nested or repeated options.
Prefers screens that feel fully populated and functional, with visible rows, actions, labels, and content rather than empty or placeholder-like states.
Prefers explicit, descriptive labels that tell the user exactly what a setting or status means.
Prefers scannable rows or list items with consistent alignment, clear affordances, and predictable structure.
Prefers imagery or illustration that supports the interface without crowding the top area or competing with controls.
Prefers light surfaces, white backgrounds, and airy compositions in non-alert contexts.
Prefers icons that are minimal, consistent, and visually unified across the screen.
Prefers onboarding or setup flows with explicit progress cues and obvious back/next navigation.
Prefers screens that include enough contextual detail to feel trustworthy and actionable, such as status, identifiers, or supporting information.
Prefers screens that focus on the core task or core settings rather than exposing too many categories or secondary options at once.
